independence.author: The same assistant wrote the product, the foundation, the oracle, the G6 to G15 holdouts, the fixes after them, the eligibility check with its G16 cashbook check, and this holdout, and knew the reader's rules when designing the stories. Prawn, the cairo application and the two XLSX writers are new to the product; the author is not. This is not a blind holdout.
independence.oracle: audit/bank-statement-foundation/oracle.py, unchanged: it reads the printed lines in the facts, the cashbook CSV and the contract, never recipe or intent, and imports nothing from the generator or the product. expected.py only runs it story by story with each story's own period.
independence.verifier: pdfminer.six, a PDF reader unrelated to the product's pdf.js, finds every printed line of the facts on its own row with all its values, and every description's words in order across the rows the writer wraps it over, Arabic in reading order glyph by glyph; and MuPDF finds no glyph drawn as .notdef (verify.py, with its own self-test of planted changes, two changed XLSX cashbooks, and a letter planted as .notdef in a Prawn simple TrueType font, a cairo Type0 font and a cairo simple TrueType font).
independence.eligibility: audit/bank-statement-eligibility/eligibility.py, run on the frozen files before the seal with MuPDF, the raw content streams and the Python standard library, never the product: every refusal the reader declares that it can check, the reading by columns (G13), each font's ToUnicode map as the prepared PDF.js reads it (G15), each XLSX cashbook as the product reads it (G16), the rules each statement exercises, and the decision story's case and outstanding item. Its report, ELIGIBILITY.json, is sealed and bound to the PDF hashes.
independence.generator: stories.py is a ninth lineage: a food distributor's operating account driven by a xoshiro128** generator seeded by SplitMix32; nothing is imported from the foundation's stories.mjs or from the G6 to G15 holdouts. common.py and expected.py are copied from G15.
independence.drafts: While the stories and writers were drafted, their PDFs and workbooks were read with pdfminer.six, MuPDF (text, glyph ids and page images), the eligibility check and its cashbook check only. No script that reads a file with the product's reader was run on any draft (DEV-61).
independence.notTuned: No product code changed between the start of G17 and the seal, and the product read none of these files.

eligibility.decided: before any product run on these files
eligibility.why: Every statement stays inside the contract: its headings, labels, footer, line kinds, number and date formats and matching policy; every cashbook keeps the six declared headings on one sheet. The writer, font, table style, geometry, period, furniture and story are what the contract leaves open. The eligibility check found nothing in any of the twelve statements that the reader declares a reason to refuse, read every one by its columns and every font's ToUnicode map as the prepared PDF.js reads it, and read both XLSX cashbooks as the product reads them, every entry (ELIGIBILITY.json). So a refusal of a positive is not a correct one unless it is for a reason no check before the seal covers, which the report then names.
eligibility.exercised: As ELIGIBILITY.json counts them: dates read with their segments reversed in the Arabic statements with Arabic-Indic digits (V07, V08, V12); values placed in their columns by the end edge of a right-aligned heading in the English statements whose headings are right-aligned; V03's cashbook read with typed amounts and dates, V10's as text.
draftFindings: The first cairo draft drew a full grid's column edges through the control lines, whose label spans the first four columns, so that a label crossed a rule; the reader refuses text a rule meets. The grid now draws each row's own edges and leaves out the interior edges of a spanned row.

In the first Arabic draft a SADAD reference in Readex Pro at 7.2 points was wider than its column and, starting at the cell's right edge, ran into the withdrawal column. The reference column was widened.

The first cairo drafts drew V08's continuation across the first four columns, so that its first word stood in no column: the eligibility check stopped V08 at page 2, line 6 (COLUMN). A continuation continues the description above it; it is now drawn in the description column, by Prawn as well. Drawn there, the first text wrapped over two rows; it was shortened to one.
fastexcel stamps docProps/core.xml with the clock's time and has no setting for it: two renders differed in that part alone. It is left as the writer writes it and recorded here.

With the Arabic file holding no hyphen, a date in Arabic-Indic digits is drawn as five runs from two fonts; the eligibility check reads it with its segments reversed (reversedDate) rather than as touching runs joined.

browserDecision.why: The browser run accepts the first acceptable case of one story and the export checker's self-test alters that story's workbook. V01 has a case the page accepts (date-gap) and items outstanding on both sides, so every alteration has a target; ELIGIBILITY.json checks it. If the product refuses V01, the next of V07 (date-gap, an item outstanding) and V02 (amount-date-suggestion, an item outstanding) it does not refuse is decided.

attribution.what: After the first run, the same package is run on the product as it was before G16 (79b8e4c: the cashbook reader did not yet refuse a row whose cells the generic reader flags) and recorded beside it, so that a difference in V03's or V10's XLSX cashbook says whether G16's refusal changed the outcome on writers it was not measured on. It is a diagnostic, not a second result.

rules: rectangle traced back to its start
ablation.what: After the first run, on the commit it ran on, each rule is switched off in a private copy of the product, one at a time, and the package run again: a positive that completes with every rule and not with one off needed it. V03's typed XLSX cashbook is written to need typed cashbook amounts; whether it does is what the ablation measures. It is a diagnostic, not a second result.

measures.reading: Every printed line read from the PDF equals the facts: kind, page, dates, reference, amounts, balances; descriptions and continuation text after NFKC and whitespace normalisation.
measures.result: The matching result, in the facts' keys, equals EXPECTED.json: automatic pairs, review groups with their reasons, both outstanding sides, timing, and held statements with their counts.
measures.capacity: Eligible positives whose result equals EXPECTED.json from upload through matching, save, restore and Excel in the browser.
measures.falseAutomatic: Automatic pairs that EXPECTED.json does not hold, over all twelve statements. Must be zero.
measures.held: A held statement is held whole, with the oracle's status, and nothing in it approved, suggested or called outstanding.
measures.refusal: A positive the product refuses, or holds without the oracle holding it, is a failed positive, never a correct abstention.
measures.cashbookAgreement: For V03 and V10, the product's reading of the XLSX cashbook equals the CSV's, and equals what the eligibility check read before the seal.

afterRun: Results are recorded as they come, with the commit they ran on. A fix made after seeing them turns this set into regression for that fix; a new claim of generalisation needs a new holdout.
